      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped;
            a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped
            from the national digits. The stored and returned value is a '+'
            followed by 8 to 15 digits (e.g. '0412 345 678' becomes
            '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional. When supplied it must
            be a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned
            lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered. Optional on create; when not
            supplied it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only flag set on create to acknowledge that this owner
            deliberately shares a household with an existing owner. When true it
            allows creating an owner whose lastName and address match an existing
            owner instead of rejecting the request with 409.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone

      title: Owner fields

      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped;
            a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped
            from the national digits. The stored and returned value is a '+'
            followed by 8 to 15 digits (e.g. '0412 345 678' becomes
            '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional. When supplied it must
            be a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned
            lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered. Optional on create; when not
            supplied it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only flag set on create to acknowledge that this owner
            deliberately shares a household with an existing owner. When true it
            allows creating an owner whose lastName and address match an existing

          example: true

## Summary

I implemented the `sharesHousehold` / `householdId` feature on `POST /api/owners`.

**Behavior:** When a request sets `sharesHousehold: true`, the controller skips the 409 conflict that normally rejects a new owner whose `lastName` + `address` match an existing owner. Every created owner is assigned a `householdId` — a stable, deterministic identifier derived from the SHA-256 of the normalized `lastName` + `address`, so any owners in the same household get the identical value. The `householdId` is persisted and returned in the owner representation.

**Changes:**
- `model/Owner.java` — added the `householdId` field (mapped to a `household_id` column) with getter/setter, mirroring the existing `customerCode` pattern.
- `rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java` — hoisted the normalized last-name/address keys, set `householdId(...)` on every create, and added a `householdId(...)` helper producing `HH-<12 upper-hex>` from `SHA-256(lastNameKey|addressKey)`. Reused the existing `normalizeIdentity` normalization so households match consistently.
- `resources/openapi.yml` — added the read-only `householdId` property to the `Owner` schema (this drives the generated `OwnerDto`, which MapStruct maps automatically by name).
- `db/{hsqldb,h2,mysql,postgres}/schema.sql` — added the `household_id` column to the `owners` table.

Test result: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — **BUILD SUCCESS**. The acceptance test confirms two `sharesHousehold` joiners at the same address/last name receive the same non-blank `householdId`.
